title: Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K
description:
Given an integer array `nums` (which may contain negative numbers, zeros, and positive numbers) and a positive integer `k`, return the length of the shortest **non-empty contiguous subarray** of `nums` whose sum is at least `k`.

If no contiguous subarray has a sum greater than or equal to `k`, return `-1`.
hints: Because `nums` can contain negative numbers, a standard two-pointer sliding window fails. Rewrite subarray sums using prefix sums `P[j] - P[i] >= k` with `i < j`.

Maintain a monotonic increasing deque of prefix sum indices. If `P[i] >= P[j]` for `i < j`, then `i` is strictly worse than `j` for all future endpoints (larger prefix sum and farther left), so pop `i` from the back.

Whenever `P[j] - P[dq[0]] >= k`, update the answer with `j - dq[0]` and pop `dq[0]` from the front because any future `j' > j` would only form a longer subarray with `dq[0]`. Use 64-bit integers (`long`) for prefix sums.

examples.explanation: The single-element subarray [1] has sum 1 >= 1 and length 1.
Even the full array [1, 2] sums to 3 < 4, so return -1.
Only the full array [2, -1, 2] reaches sum 3 >= 3, giving length 3.
